prompt:
This repository is Dispatch, an incident management platform. Someone who comes late to an incident's channel can get a machine-written briefing on what they missed. When several latecomers ask one after another, Dispatch does not always write a fresh briefing: it may hand out an earlier one again. Which function decides between handing out an earlier briefing and writing a new one, how old may a briefing be and still be handed out again, and which function finds that earlier briefing? Do not change any code.

Finish your answer with these four lines, in this exact form:
FILE: <path of the file that defines the deciding function>
FUNCTION: <name of the deciding function>
MAX_AGE: <how old a briefing may be and still be handed out again, number and unit>
LOOKUP: <name of the function that finds the earlier briefing>
notes: Answer: src/dispatch/ai/service.py, generate_read_in_summary (called by the Slack member-joined handler and the summary command), which reuses an AI read-in summary event logged within READ_IN_SUMMARY_CACHE_DURATION = 120 s (ai/constants.py), found by event/service.py get_recent_summary_event. Trap: get_recent_summary_event's own default is max_age_seconds=300 ('5 minutes default'), overridden by the caller. Lexical gap, grep -i: 'briefing', 'latecomer', 'machine-written', 'hand out', 'handed', 'how old', 'comes late' have 0 hits; 'missed' 3 (icons); 'fresh' 95 (UI refresh code); 'finds' 3; 'earlier' 1 (a conference test); 'channel' 663 lines in 82 files; 'late' is a substring of 'template' (5,000+ lines). The code says read-in summary, cache duration, event. The question avoids 'join(s)', which points at the Slack member-joined handler, 'so far', which is in the reply text, and 'recent', which is in the lookup function's name. Memory: read-in summaries were added upstream in July 2025 (#6116); the 120 s window and the lookup through the event log are too fine to recall, and the nearby 300 s default is the likely wrong pick. No plant involved.
